title: Lesson 3. U1. E&F – Personal Information + My Local Park
source: Life 2nd Edition A2-B1 Student's Book Unit 1E-1F; Track 9 extension

homework.title: Design and complete a new-student information form

screens.title: What you will be able to do

groups.heading: Personal information
items: match everyday questions to form headings

groups.heading: Listening & viewing
items: watch for sequence and key details

groups.heading: Communication
items: ask and answer about a local park

screens.title: Doctor Dash
screens.instruction: Match each medical problem with suitable advice. Then choose one pair and make a short patient–pharmacist exchange.

items.answer: Try drinking hot water with honey and lemon.
Why don't you buy some cough sweets?
You should go to bed and rest.
You need to take some medicine and see a doctor if it continues.

screens.title: Forms in everyday life
screens.instruction: Look at the four form examples. Type what each form is for. Then discuss: Which kind have you filled in before, and on what occasion?

screens.title: What is each form for?
screens.instruction: Choose the best answer for each form. Submit before the teacher checks the answers.

items.prompt: A form asks for passport number, nationality and place of birth.
A form asks about smoking, current medications and past operations.

screens.title: Information on forms
screens.instruction: Drag and drop each heading in the right box and submit your answers.

items.prompt: Are you married, single or divorced?
Do you take any pills or medicine?
How many children do you have?
What country were you born in?
What city/town were you born in?
Who can we call in your family if you need help?
What is the first letter of your middle name?

screens.title: Form conventions
screens.instruction: Work through the three questions from the Student's Book. Type your answer and submit before checking.

items.prompt: Find abbreviations on the forms. What does DOB mean?
What do Mr, Mrs, Ms and Dr mean or show?
items.answer: They are titles used before a person's name.

items.prompt: Which form tells you not to use lower-case letters?
items.answer: The form that says PLEASE USE CAPITAL LETTERS.

screens.title: New patient information
screens.instruction: The receptionist is collecting information from a new patient. Listen to the conversation and complete the three details.

items.answer: Three times a week / about three hours

screens.title: Build a new-student form
screens.instruction: Drag the information headings you think a new language-school student form needs into the blank form. Submit your design, then add sample details in the smaller spaces. Exchange and check with a partner.
checkQuestions: Is the form easy to fill in?
Do you know what to write in each part?
Would you change anything on the form?

screens.title: My local park
screens.subtitle: Video · Everyday life in an English park

screens.title: A place to meet, relax and exercise
screens.instruction: Study the park scene and caption. What clues show how people use this place? Then answer the two questions from the book.
screens.caption: A public park: green space for walking, meeting friends, relaxing and exercise.
questions: Why do people like going there?

screens.title: Words used in the video
screens.instruction: Drag and drop each meaning in the right box and submit your answers.

bank.text: a region or part of a town
a four-wheeled vehicle for a baby or small child
it isn't important and doesn't change my decision
what you can see around you
a path or small road only for people

items.answerText: it isn't important and doesn't change my decision
a four-wheeled vehicle for a baby or small child
what you can see around you
a region or part of a town

screens.title: Put the scenes in order
screens.instruction: Watch the video. Drag a–g into positions 1–7 in the order you see the scenes. Submit before checking.

choices.text: A woman is walking with her dog.
There's a large house near the park.
Two people are walking down a path.
A tractor is cutting the grass.

screens.title: People in the park
screens.instruction: Watch again. Student A completes When do you come to the park? Student B completes Why do you like coming to the park? Share your notes, complete the other column, then use Watch evidence to check.

rows.b: There are a lot of dogs for Jasmine to play with.

rows.a: every day; on sunny days at lunchtime
rows.b: It is high up and there is a beautiful view.

rows.a: when we were a young family and had children
rows.b: It has happy memories; it is nicer than walking the other way.

rows.a: goes through the park and spends time with friends
quite often / about twice a week
rows.b: likes jogging and exercising; it is quiet with lots of grass and trees

rows.a: tries to come to the park regularly
rows.b: likes the wild flowers and blossom on the trees

screens.title: Guess the person
screens.instruction: Student A chooses one person from the video but does not tell Student B. Student B asks the two questions from the video and guesses the person. Then change roles.
model: B: When do you come to the park?
A: I come here about twice a week.
B: How often do you come?
A: Quite often – usually twice a week.
frames: When do you come to the park?

screens.title: Exit check
screens.instruction: Complete the six quick checks. Keep your answers short.

items.prompt: A person you call in your family if you need help is your …

items.answer: a path or small road only for people

items.prompt: The first scene in the video ordering task is …
items.answer: A woman is walking with her dog.

items.prompt: Write one question used to ask about a park routine.
items.answer: When do you come to the park? / How often do you come?

screens.title: Can you do these now?
items: I can complete and design a simple form.
I can listen for personal details.
I can understand key park vocabulary.
I can ask and answer about a park routine.

screens.title: Design your own new-student form
screens.instruction: Create a clear new-student form from a completely blank canvas. Decide which headings are necessary and fill in invented/sample information. Do not use sensitive real personal data.

screens.title: Thank you
screens.subtitle: See you in the next Life lesson.
